note: Weights are tuned for getting past an ATS screen and then a recruiter's 20-second skim, which is where most CVs die. Impact and keyword alignment dominate because those are what actually decide a callback; formatting matters but is cheap to fix.

criteria.label: Impact and quantification
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Most bullets state an outcome with a number — money, time, volume, percentage, headcount or scale. Written as achievements, not duties.
common_failures: Bullets describe responsibilities ("Responsible for managing...") instead of results
Numbers absent entirely, or only vague intensifiers like "significantly improved"
Numbers present but with no baseline, so the scale is unreadable

scoring_anchors.18-20: Nearly every bullet has a concrete, credible metric tied to a business outcome
scoring_anchors.13-17: Roughly half the bullets are quantified; the rest are duty statements
scoring_anchors.7-12: A few numbers, mostly in one role; the CV mainly lists responsibilities
scoring_anchors.0-6: No quantification; reads as a job description rather than a record of results

criteria.label: Role and keyword alignment
criteria.what_good_looks_like: The hard skills, tools and domain language in the target job description appear naturally in the CV, especially in the top third. Job titles map recognisably to the target role.
common_failures: Uses synonyms the ATS will not match ("MS Excel modelling" when the JD says "financial modeling")
Key required skill is genuinely held but never named
Skills buried in a footer list rather than evidenced inside experience bullets

scoring_anchors.16-18: Almost every must-have from the JD appears, evidenced in context rather than just listed
scoring_anchors.11-15: Most core skills present, some only in a skills list
scoring_anchors.6-10: Several must-haves missing or phrased in non-matching language
scoring_anchors.0-5: Little overlap with the target role's vocabulary

criteria.label: ATS parseability and format
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Single column, standard section headings, text-based (not an image), consistent and parseable dates, no critical content inside tables, headers/footers or text boxes.
common_failures: Two-column layout — many parsers read straight across and scramble the text
Section headings that parsers do not recognise ("My Journey" instead of "Experience")
Dates in inconsistent formats, or only years, making tenure unclear
Contact details inside a header/footer, where some parsers drop them

scoring_anchors.11-12: Clean single column, standard headings, unambiguous dates, fully text-based
scoring_anchors.8-10: Mostly clean with one risky element
scoring_anchors.4-7: Multiple parser hazards — columns, graphics or non-standard headings
scoring_anchors.0-3: Likely to be badly mangled or rejected by an ATS

criteria.label: Clarity and concision
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Bullets are one to two lines, start with a strong past-tense action verb, and carry one idea each. No filler, no throat-clearing.
common_failures: Bullets running to four or five lines
Passive voice ("was responsible for", "was tasked with")
Repeating the same opening verb across many bullets
Corporate filler — "leveraged synergies", "spearheaded initiatives"

scoring_anchors.11-12: Every bullet is tight, active and single-idea
scoring_anchors.8-10: Generally tight with a few long or passive bullets
scoring_anchors.4-7: Frequently wordy or passive; hard to skim
scoring_anchors.0-3: Dense paragraphs; a recruiter cannot skim this in 20 seconds

criteria.label: Structure and completeness
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Contact details complete and reachable. Sections in the order a reader needs them for this role. Length fits experience — one page under ~8 years, two pages beyond. Reverse-chronological.
common_failures: Missing phone, email, city or LinkedIn URL
Education above experience for an experienced candidate, or vice versa for a fresher
Three pages for five years of experience
No summary where the career pivot needs explaining

scoring_anchors.9-10: Complete, correctly ordered for this candidate, right length
scoring_anchors.7-8: Complete but ordering or length is slightly off
scoring_anchors.4-6: A section missing, or noticeably too long
scoring_anchors.0-3: Key contact details or whole sections absent

criteria.label: Evidence and credibility
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Claims are specific and checkable — named tools, real scope, concrete deliverables. Seniority claimed matches evidence shown.
common_failures: Unverifiable superlatives ("best performer", "expert-level")
Claimed leadership with no team size or scope
Long tool lists with no evidence any were used seriously
Metrics implausible for the role's level

scoring_anchors.9-10: Every significant claim is specific and independently plausible
scoring_anchors.7-8: Mostly specific, a few unsupported assertions

criteria.label: Progression and narrative
criteria.what_good_looks_like: The sequence of roles tells a coherent story with visible growth in scope. Gaps and pivots are accounted for rather than left as questions.
common_failures: Unexplained multi-month gaps
Lateral moves with no growth in scope
A pivot the reader cannot make sense of without asking

scoring_anchors.7-8: Clear upward trajectory; any gap or pivot is explained
scoring_anchors.5-6: Reasonable but with one open question
scoring_anchors.3-4: Choppy history a screener will query
scoring_anchors.0-2: Incoherent sequence or large unexplained gaps

criteria.label: Language quality
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Sounds like a competent human wrote it about their own work. No AI-generated cadence, no cliché stacking, no buzzword padding. Consistent tense and person.
common_failures: AI-slop patterns — "It's not just X, it's Y", "a testament to", "pivotal moment"
Buzzword stacking with no content ("dynamic, results-driven, detail-oriented professional")
Mixed tense or first/third person within a section
Typos and inconsistent capitalisation of tool names

scoring_anchors.9-10: Clean, specific, human. No slop patterns.
scoring_anchors.7-8: Largely clean with a few clichés
scoring_anchors.4-6: Noticeably generic or AI-sounding in places
scoring_anchors.0-3: Reads as machine-generated or buzzword soup

bands.label: Strong
bands.meaning: Ready to send. Tailor keywords per application and go.

bands.label: Solid
bands.meaning: Competitive. Fixing the top two or three items should tip most screens.

bands.label: Needs work
bands.meaning: Will pass some ATS filters but rarely survive a recruiter skim.

bands.label: Weak
bands.meaning: Likely filtered before a human reads it. Rewrite the experience bullets first.

bands.label: Rebuild
bands.meaning: Start from the structure and rewrite around quantified outcomes.
